title: Circle Angle Vocabulary Practice
description: Practice defining and identifying central angles, arcs, chords, secants, and tangents.

questions.question: Which description defines a central angle?
options: An angle whose vertex is outside the circle
An angle whose vertex is at the center of the circle
A line that touches the circle once
A segment with endpoints on the circle
questions.explanation: A central angle has its vertex at the center of the circle.

questions.question: A segment has both endpoints on a circle. What is it called?
questions.explanation: A chord is a segment whose endpoints both lie on the circle.

questions.question: A tangent line intersects a circle at exactly two points.
questions.explanation: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. A secant intersects it at two points.

questions.question: Fill in the vocabulary word: A connected part of the circle's curved edge is an ____.
questions.explanation: An arc is a curved part of a circle.

questions.question: Which object is a secant?
options: A line that cuts a circle at two points
A line that touches a circle at one point
A curved part of a circle
An angle with vertex at the center
questions.explanation: A secant is a line that intersects a circle at two points.

questions.question: Every diameter is also a chord.
questions.explanation: A diameter is a chord that passes through the center of the circle.

questions.question: A line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a ____.
questions.explanation: A tangent line has exactly one point of contact with the circle.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a secant and a tangent in one or two sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: A secant intersects a circle at two points, while a tangent touches a circle at exactly one point.
questions.explanation: The key difference is the number of intersection points with the circle.
